metadata.title: The Madison Archetype Project
notes: PROJECT PROGRESS update at the planning/scoping stage. HONESTY IS THE CONSTRAINT: no beat shows tool output, because there is no tool yet. B08's schema is captioned as a design target; B07's Everyman/Ruler tension is captioned as an illustrative example of the class of finding, not a produced result; B10 exists solely to state status including 'build not started' and 'no results yet'.

Register is Plain (runtime/prose/plain/PROSE.md). Six moves sequenced: stake first (B00/B01), wrong guess built then broken (B03 -> B04 -> B07), mechanism once with EXACTLY ONE inference flag (B05, on how much personality real artefacts encode), one running example planted early and paid off late (the luxury handbag, B04 -> B07), failure modes both directions (B07 resolver + B10 limits), one compressible sentence (BVDT).
Plain does not judge the design - that is Teardown. No beat rates competing tools as badly designed; B03 describes what they do and stops.
REUSE ONLY - no new components were built for this reel. Every scene was already registered and rendering cleanly.
Slot-1 kicker is the FIXED channel series name 'Irreducibly Human' (runtime/qc/brand_labels.json, beat_lint rule 7); the per-video subject lives in the `segment` slot.

B01 triggerWords is a SINGLE TOKEN ('quiz'). buildActs() in BrutalistHesitantWriter matches triggers per whitespace-delimited token, so a multi-word trigger silently never fires - see the llm-function-calling BUILD-LOG.

B02 ChipGrid runs cols=3 with NO caption: 12 chips at cols=4 overflow to x0=-29 (edge bleed), and at cols=3 the fourth row (582-678) collides with the caption slot (~598). The clarifier moved to the spark line.
Outro is FnCallTitleOutro (no mascot, no subline): OUTRO-LOCK.md scopes the @NikBearBrown card to that channel only.

Narrator is named on screen and in voice as Prashanth: B00's narration opens "Hi, my name is Prashanth...", so the greeting slot reads Prashanth rather than the channel's Liam persona. Keeping 'Liam' would put the picture in direct contradiction with the audio on the cold open.

metadata.review_labels=false suppresses the beat-marker footer overlay on the review cut (per feedback: no review label on the output). It is the symmetric opposite of the existing keep_review_labels flag and is honoured only on the review path, so masters are unaffected.

BVDT artifactLines must contain NO empty strings: ClaudeVerdictArtifact numbers every line and does not filter blanks, so a blank used as a visual spacer renders as an orphan number (shipped as '4.' with no text in the first cut).

skin_warnings: BOUT: palette=claude but the outro is 'FnCallTitleOutro' — OUTRO LAW wants ClaudeTitleOutro

beats.narration_text: Hi, my name is Prashanth, and this video is a progress update on my Madison project, a brand-archetype analyzer. Brand archetypes are an old idea: twelve personality patterns a brand can occupy. There is no shortage of tools that name yours. I am building one anyway, because naming is the part that helps least. Here is where it stands.

shot.new_visual_element: the composer answering what the project is and how far along it is
shot.visual_intent: COLD OPEN LAW - opens on the Claude UI and the ask lands answered. The output lines answer 'what are you building / how far along', NOT an archetype result: there is no tool yet, so showing one would be fabrication

beats.narration_text: I'm scoping a brand-archetype analyzer. It reads your real evidence, and it ends in decisions. Today it is a plan and a scope document, not a working tool. That distinction matters.

shot.new_visual_element: the overview written, reconsidered, and corrected on screen
shot.visual_intent: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW - the whole idea in one breath. The correction is the reel's actual misconception: a viewer arrives expecting another archetype QUIZ, and 'quiz' is incompatible with the two lines that follow, so the writer fixes the category

show.event: 0.8s of silence - the caret blinks on an empty cream page before the voice starts
writer types 'I'm scoping a brand-archetype quiz.' - 'quiz' turns terracotta, marked for deletion
a full beat of hesitation, then 'quiz' deletes
'analyzer' types in its place
the two remaining lines type in: 'It reads your real evidence' / 'and ends in decisions.'
corrected sentence holds on screen through the cut

props.text:
I'm scoping a brand-archetype quiz.
It reads your real evidence

beats.narration_text: The framework is Jung's, borrowed by branding: twelve archetypes. Hero. Sage. Ruler. Creator. Caregiver. Everyman. Jester. Lover. Rebel. Magician. Innocent. Explorer. Each one is a personality a brand can occupy, a consistent way of speaking, promising, and behaving. Twelve slots. That is the whole vocabulary.

shot.new_visual_element: all twelve archetypes as a chip grid
shot.visual_intent: FRAMEWORK beat - the whole vocabulary on screen BEFORE any example, so every later beat lands against a whole the viewer already holds. Named in narration order so each chip lands on its spoken word

show.event: chips land one per spoken archetype, left to right, three per row
row two fills: Creator, Caregiver, Everyman
row three fills: Jester, Lover, Rebel
row four completes: Magician, Innocent, Explorer - all twelve now held together
grid holds still while the voice names what an archetype actually is

beats.narration_text: Here is what most archetype tools actually do. You fill in a short brief, a few adjectives about how you see yourself. It returns one label. You are the Sage. Then a generic paragraph about what Sages are like. Three steps, and every one of them runs on what you already believed.

shot.new_visual_element: the shallow pipeline as three stacked cards
shot.visual_intent: Plain move 2 - build the wrong guess before the right one. Nothing is accented: none of these three steps is the answer, and the caption carries the judgement-free observation that the loop is closed on the user's own input

show.event: card one stacks in: a short self-report brief
card two stacks under it: one label out
card three stacks: a generic paragraph
caption settles under the stack - the input and the output are the same belief

layers.title: a short brief
layers.sub: a few adjectives about how you see yourself

layers.title: a generic paragraph
layers.sub: what Sages are like, in general

props.caption: every step runs on what you already believed — the evidence never enters

beats.narration_text: So predict this one before I go on. A brand sells a four thousand dollar handbag. Its ads talk like your funniest friend: casual, self-deprecating, one of us. Which archetype is that brand actually signalling? Commit to an answer. I'll come back to it.

shot.new_visual_element: predict card - the viewer commits before the reveal
shot.visual_intent: Plain move 4 - plants the ONE running example, specific enough to visualise, to be paid off at B07. The commit line is the single accent

show.event: question card fades up on the cream stage
the two competing readings sit side by side, ink on cream, neither highlighted
commit line appears in terracotta - the one accent - asking for an answer now
card holds still, giving the viewer real time to choose

props.question: A $4,000 handbag, advertised like your funniest friend. Which archetype is it actually signalling?
props.commit: commit to an answer before the next beat

beats.narration_text: First commitment: read the evidence, not the self-report. The inputs are a brand's actual published language and its actual visuals, the words it ships and the images it chooses. One flag: how much of a personality those artefacts really encode is the open question of this project, and it is why I need samples before I need code.

shot.new_visual_element: the brand's own artefacts flowing into the analyzer
shot.visual_intent: Plain move 3 - the mechanism once, plainly, with EXACTLY ONE inference flag, placed where 'how much personality artefacts encode' is doing real work. It is also the honest seam of the whole project

show.event: dark rack labelled 'the brand's own artefacts' builds on the left
three artefact chips fly along the arc into the analyzer window: published copy, product pages, the visual system
the window's task line reads 'which archetype is this, on the evidence?'
chips check off as they land; the first is the single terracotta accent
settle line reads: samples before code

props.destTitle: which archetype is this, on the evidence?
props.arcCaption: what the brand ships — never self-reported adjectives

beats.narration_text: Back to that handbag. Here is the prompt I use to map where a brand contradicts itself.

shot.new_visual_element: the composer with the generation prompt for the next beat's figure
shot.visual_intent: ASK->RESULT LAW - the tension figure at B07 is preceded by the actual prompt that produces it, so the pair reads as a receipt

show.event: composer card fades up under the spark line 'Map the tension.'
the generation prompt types in
send arms terracotta; running indicator reads 'mapping the tension...'

props.command: Read this brand's copy and its pricing as two separate signals. Name the archetype each one points to, and what the gap costs.

beats.narration_text: The honest answer is both, and that is the point. The content reads Everyman: approachable, one of us. The pricing signals Ruler: exclusive, in command. Neither reading is wrong. The brand is sending two personalities at once, and that inconsistency is what costs it trust. A single label would have hidden it.

shot.new_visual_element: one brand splitting into two archetype readings, resolved by the cost
shot.visual_intent: WORKED EXAMPLE and Plain move 5 - pays off B04's prediction and states both directions: neither reading is wrong, and the failure is the gap between them. Captioned as an ILLUSTRATIVE example of the class of finding, not a produced result

show.event: the single brand question splits into two branches
left branch fills: the copy reads Everyman - approachable, one of us
right branch fills: the pricing signals Ruler - exclusive, in command
both branches converge on one resolver card in terracotta: the gap is what costs trust
resolver holds - a single label would have hidden the whole finding

beats.narration_text: Second and third commitments. Return a primary and a secondary archetype, and flag the tension between them. Then do not stop at diagnosis. This is the output I am designing toward: messaging pillars, tone guardrails, and the shadow, the way this archetype fails when it overplays itself. Decisions, not a label.

shot.new_visual_element: the planned output schema as a code block
shot.visual_intent: the deliverable made concrete and READABLE on screen while the voice reacts to it. Title and trailing comment both mark it a DESIGN TARGET - nothing here was produced by a tool, because no tool exists yet

the tension field lands, carrying the Everyman/Ruler gap from the previous beat
messaging pillars and tone guardrails list in
the shadow field lands last - the trap the archetype falls into when overplayed

props.title: planned output schema — a design target, not produced

beats.narration_text: Twelve archetypes is too much to build at once, so I am not. I am starting with Ruler, and only Ruler. The team's work is in luxury branding, which is where Ruler lives, so it is the archetype I can get real samples for and real feedback on. The rest waits.

shot.visual_intent: the scoping decision made visible and ordered. Only the first layer is accented - it is the only one being built, and the other two are explicitly deferred

layer two stacks under it in plain ink: the adjacent luxury archetypes, later
layer three stacks: the remaining nine, not scheduled
caption settles - the reason is sample access, not preference

beats.narration_text: So where this actually is. The scope is agreed with the team. I am coordinating on gathering brand voice and visual samples to train and test against. The build has not started. There are no results yet, and anything I showed you as output was a design target, not a finding.

shot.new_visual_element: the five-chip status board, including what is NOT done
shot.visual_intent: the honesty beat. Two of the five chips are negative on purpose - 'build not started' and 'no results yet' - so the status board cannot be read as a progress brag. This is also the falsifiability beat: it names what would have to exist before any claim could be made

show.event: chip one lands: scope agreed with the team
chip two: gathering brand voice samples
chip three: gathering visual samples
chip four lands plainly: build not started
chip five: no results yet
caption settles under the board - what was shown was a target, not a finding

props.caption: planning stage — everything shown as output was a design target, not a finding

beats.narration_text: The sentence worth repeating: an archetype is only useful once it constrains a decision. Everything I am building serves that. Evidence instead of self-report. A pair instead of a label. Guardrails instead of a paragraph. None of it is built yet. That is the honest status.

shot.new_visual_element: artifact page holding the compressible sentence and the status
shot.visual_intent: Plain move 6 - one sentence that stays true if it is the only thing repeated secondhand, compressing the DISTINCTION rather than the topic. The status line is on the page so the summary cannot be quoted as a capability claim

show.event: artifact page opens in the Claude window
the one-line claim lands first and largest: an archetype is only useful once it constrains a decision
the three substitutions list under it, in order
the last line holds alone: scoped, not built

props.artifactHeading: An archetype is only useful once it constrains a decision.
artifactLines: Evidence instead of self-report — read what the brand ships.
A pair instead of a label — primary, secondary, and the tension.
Guardrails instead of a paragraph — pillars, tone, and the shadow.
Status: scoped with the team. Not built. No results yet.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this: take a brand I name, quote five lines of its actual published copy and describe three of its actual visuals, then argue a primary and a secondary archetype from that evidence alone, and name where the two contradict each other. Then check three things. Does it quote real copy, not vibes. Does it commit to a second archetype. And is the contradiction actionable. Run it on a brand you know well.

shot.new_visual_element: the composer with the viewer's prompt and the three-point rubric beside it
shot.visual_intent: HANDOFF LAW plus nopunt SCAFFOLDED TASK - the prompt is read aloud verbatim then discussed, and the rubric lets the viewer judge the output instead of admiring it. It also has the viewer run the method by hand, which is the honest thing to offer while the tool does not exist

show.event: greeting reads 'Your turn.' - the one greeting that drops the persona
the prompt types into the composer as the voice reads it word for word
running indicator reads 'paste this into Claude...'
rubric item 1 lands: does it quote real copy, not vibes
rubric item 2 lands: does it commit to a SECOND archetype
rubric item 3 lands: is the contradiction actionable

props.command: Take a brand I name. Quote five lines of its actual published copy and describe three of its actual visuals. Then argue a primary AND a secondary archetype from that evidence alone — and name where the two contradict each other.
output: Check the answer against three things:
1. does it quote real copy, or just describe vibes?
2. does it commit to a SECOND archetype, not just one?
3. is the contradiction it names something you could act on?

beats.narration_text: That's the Madison archetype project. More soon.
